_comment: Networking tasks for the topology templates in vm_topologies.json. 'check_node' names the node whose SSH connection runs 'check' (a bash script; exit code 0 = pass) after the agent's turn (or on demand, via 'Score now'). Every node's first network interface is NAT/setup-only and already has an address - never touch it; its other interfaces are the lab links, with no address until configured. ids must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$.

tasks.title: Address two hosts on one switch
tasks.prompt: This lab has two hosts, h1 and h2, connected through one switch, sw1 (already working as a plain Ethernet switch - it needs no configuration). Addressing plan: h1 = 10.0.0.11/24, h2 = 10.0.0.12/24, same /24 network. On h1 and h2, find the lab-facing interface (run `ip link`; it is NOT the one that already has an address - leave that one alone), bring it up and assign the given address with `ip addr add <address>/24 dev <interface>`. When done, h1 must be able to ping h2.

tasks.title: Address a LAN with a switch and an idle router
tasks.prompt: h1, h2 and r1 all sit on one switch, sw1 (already working, no configuration needed). Addressing plan: h1 = 10.0.0.11/24, h2 = 10.0.0.12/24, r1's interface on this LAN = 10.0.0.1/24. On each of h1, h2 and r1, find the lab-facing interface (run `ip link`; leave the one that already has an address alone), bring it up and assign the given address with `ip addr add <address>/24 dev <interface>`. When done, h1 must be able to ping h2 directly (they're on the same LAN, so r1 isn't on the path yet - just get it addressed too).

tasks.title: Route between two LANs through one router
tasks.prompt: Two LANs, each with its own switch (sw1, sw2 - already working, no configuration needed), joined by one router, r1. Addressing plan: h1 = 10.0.1.11/24 (gateway 10.0.1.1), on sw1's LAN; h2 = 10.0.2.11/24 (gateway 10.0.2.1), on sw2's LAN; r1 has one interface on each LAN - assign 10.0.1.1/24 to the one facing sw1 and 10.0.2.1/24 to the one facing sw2. Use `ip link`/`ip addr` on each node to find its lab-facing interface(s) (leave any interface that already has an address alone). On r1, enable IP forwarding: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1`. On h1 and h2, set the given address and a default route via the given gateway: `ip route add default via <gateway>`. When done, h1 must be able to ping h2.

tasks.title: Route between two LANs through two routers
tasks.prompt: Two LANs, each with its own switch (sw1, sw2 - already working, no configuration needed), joined by two routers, r1 and r2, over a point-to-point link between them. Addressing plan: h1 = 10.0.1.11/24 (gateway 10.0.1.1), on sw1's LAN; h2 = 10.0.2.11/24 (gateway 10.0.2.1), on sw2's LAN; r1's LAN-facing interface = 10.0.1.1/24; the r1<->r2 transit link = 10.0.0.1/30 on r1's side, 10.0.0.2/30 on r2's side; r2's LAN-facing interface = 10.0.2.1/24. Use `ip link`/`ip addr` on each node to find its lab-facing interface(s) (leave any interface that already has an address alone; a router here has two lab interfaces). Assign exactly these addresses. Enable IP forwarding on r1 and r2 (`sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1`). Add the static route each router needs for the OTHER router's LAN (e.g. on r1: `ip route add 10.0.2.0/24 via 10.0.0.2`). On h1 and h2, set the given address and default gateway. When done, h1 must be able to ping h2.

tasks.title: Load-balance two backends behind nginx
tasks.prompt: client, web1, web2 and lb1 all sit on one switch, sw1 (already working, no configuration needed), on 10.0.5.0/24. Addressing plan: client = 10.0.5.10/24, web1 = 10.0.5.11/24, web2 = 10.0.5.12/24, lb1 = 10.0.5.1/24. On each node, find its lab-facing interface with `ip link` (leave the one that already has an address alone) and assign the given address. On web1 and web2, write a small index.html identifying which host it is, then start a backend on port 8080, e.g. `cd /tmp && echo 'web1' > index.html && python3 -m http.server 8080 &` (use 'web2' on web2). On lb1 (nginx is already installed and running), add a `stream {}` block to /etc/nginx/nginx.conf with an `upstream` pointing at 10.0.5.11:8080 and 10.0.5.12:8080 and a `server { listen 80; proxy_pass <upstream>; }`, then `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`. When done, a request from client to lb1 on port 80 must succeed.

tasks.title: Route between two LANs through a default-drop firewall
tasks.prompt: Two LANs, each with its own switch (sw1, sw2 - already working, no configuration needed), joined by one firewall appliance, fw1 (nftables is installed and enabled, but its ruleset is still at Ubuntu's permissive default - this is a real firewall you must lock down, not a router). Addressing plan: h1 = 10.0.3.11/24 (gateway 10.0.3.1), on sw1's LAN; h2 = 10.0.4.11/24 (gateway 10.0.4.1), on sw2's LAN; fw1 has one interface on each LAN - assign 10.0.3.1/24 to the one facing sw1 and 10.0.4.1/24 to the one facing sw2. Use `ip link`/`ip addr` on each node to find its lab-facing interface(s). On fw1, enable IP forwarding (`sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1`), then configure nftables with a default-DROP forward policy and an explicit rule accepting only ICMP between the two LANs (e.g. a filter table with a forward chain, `policy drop`, and `ip protocol icmp accept`), then apply it (`nft -f` your ruleset file, or `nft add` the rules directly). On h1 and h2, set the given address and default gateway. When done, h1 must be able to ping h2 - which only works if forwarding is on AND the ICMP-accept rule is actually in place.

tasks.title: Route between two LANs with OSPF
tasks.prompt: Two LANs, each with its own switch (sw1, sw2 - already working, no configuration needed), joined by two routers, r1 and r2, over a point-to-point link between them. Addressing plan: h1 = 192.168.1.11/24 (gateway 192.168.1.1), on sw1's LAN; h2 = 192.168.2.11/24 (gateway 192.168.2.1), on sw2's LAN; r1's LAN-facing interface = 192.168.1.1/24; the r1<->r2 transit link = 192.168.12.1/30 on r1's side, 192.168.12.2/30 on r2's side; r2's LAN-facing interface = 192.168.2.1/24. Use `ip link`/`ip addr` on each node to find its lab-facing interface(s) (leave any interface that already has an address alone; a router here has two lab interfaces). Assign exactly these addresses and enable IP forwarding on both routers. Do NOT add static routes between the LANs: run OSPF (area 0) on r1 and r2 with FRR (`vtysh` on the routers) so each router learns the other router's LAN. On h1 and h2, set the given address and default gateway. When done, r1 and r2 must be OSPF neighbors in the Full state, and h1 must be able to ping h2.

tasks.title: Router-on-a-stick with two VLANs
tasks.prompt: One switch (sw1) connects two hosts and a router. Put the hosts in separate VLANs and route between them on a single router link (router-on-a-stick). sw1's lab ports: enp0s8 connects to h1, enp0s9 to h2, enp0s10 to r1. On sw1, turn VLAN filtering on for br0, make enp0s8 an access port in VLAN 10 and enp0s9 an access port in VLAN 20 (each untagged, with that VLAN as its PVID, and no longer in VLAN 1), and make enp0s10 a trunk carrying VLANs 10 and 20 tagged. On r1, create two 802.1Q subinterfaces on its lab interface: VLAN 10 with 192.168.10.1/24 and VLAN 20 with 192.168.20.1/24, and enable IP forwarding. On h1 set 192.168.10.11/24 with gateway 192.168.10.1, and on h2 set 192.168.20.11/24 with gateway 192.168.20.1, both untagged on their lab interface. When done, h1 must be able to ping h2 through r1.

tasks.title: Run DHCP and DNS for a LAN
tasks.prompt: One LAN on switch sw1 (already working) with two hosts and a server, srv1, which has dnsmasq installed but not configured or running. Give srv1's lab interface the static address 192.168.50.1/24. Configure dnsmasq on srv1 (in a new file in /etc/dnsmasq.d/) to hand out addresses 192.168.50.100-192.168.50.150 by DHCP with a 1-hour lease, and to serve DNS for the domain "lab": srv1.lab must resolve to 192.168.50.1, and each DHCP client must be resolvable by its hostname under .lab (h1.lab, h2.lab). Start dnsmasq. On h1 and h2, get an address for the lab interface by DHCP (`dhclient <interface>`); don't set their addresses by hand. When done, h1 must hold a DHCP address in that range, resolve srv1.lab and h2.lab through srv1, and reach h2.

tasks.title: Give a LAN internet access through NAT
tasks.prompt: h1 sits on a LAN (switch sw1, already working) behind router r1, whose other link goes to up1, an upstream node standing in for the internet: up1's side of that link is already 198.51.100.1/30, and it serves a web page at http://203.0.113.10/. up1 has no route to your LAN. r1's lab interfaces: enp0s8 connects to sw1 (the LAN), enp0s9 to up1. Give r1 192.168.60.1/24 on the LAN side and 198.51.100.2/30 on the upstream side, a default route via 198.51.100.1, IP forwarding, and source NAT (masquerade) for traffic from 192.168.60.0/24 leaving towards up1. Give h1 192.168.60.11/24 with gateway 192.168.60.1. When done, h1 must be able to fetch http://203.0.113.10/ and ping it.
